newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs edge up in Tokyo, summit has little impact.
newsitem.headline: JGBs edge up in Tokyo, summit has little impact.

text.p: The benchmark 10-year September Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract edged higher on short-covering in early morning Tokyo, but the topside was expected to be limited by dollar gains against the yen, traders said.

The Group of Seven (G7) summit ended with an economic statement that was largely within the market's expectations, helping the dollar rise to above 115 yen in early trade compared to 114.80/90 yen at Friday's New York close.
These gains were likely to make it difficult for the key September to rise much above 124, traders said.
"The key contract failed to break above 124 on Friday, both in Tokyo and overseas, and is unlikely to rise much today as well, given current market factors," one trader said.

He noted, and others agreed, that the bond market was much more interested in the auction of 10-year bonds planned for Tuesday and Wednesday's release of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" quarterly report of business sentiment. Most operators were expected to sideline themselves on Monday, traders said.
"Everyone wants to see the tankan before deciding what action they want to take," one trader with a long-term credit bank said.

In Denver on Sunday, Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said that Japan's trade surplus was unlikely to rise significantly in the medium term, but declined to address the impact of current foreign exchange rates on efforts to limit Japan's surplus. However, he added that Japan would not accept wild swings in the yen's exchange rate.

U.S. President Bill Clinton warned Japan that a return to "exploding" trade surpluses with the United States would hurt both countries. He added that the decision by the Japanese government to try to pursue a path of fiscal austerity ran the risk of going back to an old export-driven strategy of growth.
